mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reflects an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 4.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes economic contraction and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 211.0), elevated federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) signal aggressive monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 211.0 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200 thousand units signals a contraction in the residential construction sector, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST < 1200.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a broad-based economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where both INDPRO and PAYEMS decline, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.8% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a recession and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.8, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A retail sales level (RSAFS) above 386000 million dollars signals robust consumer spending, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS > 386000.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.
